must_remember: A Ramsden eyepiece consists of two plano-convex lenses of equal focal lengths ($f_1 = f_2 = f$) with their curved surfaces facing each other.
The separation between the field lens and the eye lens is maintained at $d = \frac{2}{3}f$ to satisfy the condition for minimum spherical aberration.
The equivalent focal length of the Ramsden eyepiece is $F = \frac{3}{4}f$.
The focal plane lies outside the field lens at a distance of $f/4$, allowing the incorporation of cross-hairs and micrometers.
Ramsden's condition for achromatism when both lenses are made of the same glass is $d = \frac{f_1 + f_2}{2}$.

glossary.meaning: The lens in an eyepiece placed closer to the objective lens of the optical instrument.
The lens in an eyepiece closest to the observer's eye.
The focal length of a single thin lens that would produce the same optical effect as the lens combination: $F = \frac{3f}{4}$.
The condition $d = \frac{f_1 + f_2}{2}$ for lenses made of the same material to prevent chromatic variation of focal length.
The image of the objective formed by the eyepiece where the emergent rays converge to a minimum cross-section.
